newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - AUGUST 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - AUGUST 8.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- BANK TALKS THE POUND DOWN

The Bank of England's monetary policy committee voted to increase base interest rates, for the fourth consecutive month, by a quarter of a percentage point to seven per cent, its highest rate since 1992. The bank commented that the raise would probably be enough to meet the chancellors target for inflation of 2.5 per cent for the next two years.
-- PITCHER PRESSED ON EXECUTIVE ROLE AT UNITED

Some leading institutional shareholders of United Utilities, the company which owns North West Water NWW.L and Norweb, are telling excective director Sir Peter Middleton that the executive chairman, Sir Desmond Pitcher, should step down and become a non-executive chairman of the company prior to his planned departure in 2000. Major shareholders, of at least eight in number, are apparently completely divided on the decision.
-- ASIA FEARS TAMAGOTCHI PETS ARE BECOMING VIRTUAL PESTS

Political leaders in China, South Korea, Singapore and the Philipines have all recently complained sincerly that the egg-shaped electronic tamagotchi "pets" are a malign influence on Asia's infants, with national bans in schools in South Korea and parts of Thailand and Hong Kong. Japanese toymaker Bandai's new elcetronic pet is predicted to sell 40 million by March 1998.
-- MMC CHAIRMAN IS TO RETIRE 15 MONTHS EARLY

The Monopolies and Mergers Commission chairman, Sir Graeme Odgers has announced plans to retire 15 months before the end of his contract following plans by the government to reform the laws of UK competition and to restructure the MMC to make a more powerful Competition Commission. Sir Graeme denied any rift between himself and the trade and industry secretary, Margaret Beckett.
-- RUSSIAN BANK EYES LAST BIG OIL COMPANY

In an interview with the Financial Times, Vladimir Potanin, president of Russia's Oneximbank group, has revealed the bank's intention to purchase Russia's last state-owned oil company, Rosneft, when it is privatised for as much as $1bn or more later this year. The decision follows Oneximbank's purchases in the last fortnight which include government stakes in the mining group Norilsk Nickel and in Svyazinvest, the telecoms holding company.
-- APPLE'S SHARE RISE CONTINUES IN WAKE OF MICROSOFT DEAL

Following the news of Microsofts $150m stake in Apple computers and the two companies intentions to merge products, shares in Apple continued to rise yesterday closing up $2.875 to $29.2475 per share. Apple plan to include more Microsoft software on their computers and Microsoft have pledged to create
more packages for Apple computers.
-- WINDFALLS HAVE LITTLE EFFECT ON SPENDING

The Confederation of British Industry revealed the results of its latest distributive trades survey that indicate that annual growth in retail sales dropped slightly last month, compared to June, contrary to the expected boom from the 22bn stg in windfall payouts during the month. HSBC economist, Jonathon Loynes, commented that the news indicates the relatively short-term effect of the demutualised payouts.
-- LABOUR APPROVES GAS-FIRED POWER STATION

Government minister for science, energy and industry, John Battle has given his first approval to plans to build a power station, this one being a 300m stg gas- fired power station to be built by Entergy Power Group at the BP Chemicals' Saltend refinery. Mr Battle wished to demonstrate the governments intention to improve both the economic and the environmental management of energy.
-- SMITHKLINE HANDS OVER PATENTS TO SPIN-OFF

The UK's second biggest pharmaceutical company SmithKline Beecham is creating a new spin-off biotechnology company from its technology sector by handing over a portfolio of patents and some laboratory equipment in return for a 10 per cent stake in the Adprotech company that is being funded with 5m stg and 55 per cent owned by venture capital companies 3i, Alta Berkeley and the Prelude Trust.
-- AUDITOR DROPS EIDOS OVER LAPSES IN GOVERNANCE

Big Six audit company Coopers & Lybrand said that it would not stand for a fourth year of reappointment as auditor at the world's third-largest developer of computer games, Eidos, because of "certain inadequacies in the company's corporate governance practices" which fail to reach the code laid down in the Cadbury report. The news comes as Sir Robert Hampel published his corporate governance report earlier this week. For a full range of news monitoring services, phone BMC "44-171-377-1742
